paragraphs: 3rd Eye sells modular, subscription-based software that runs on top of its own heavy-duty truck camera systems. Its buyers are waste hauling companies that have to manage collection fleets safely and stay connected to their customers. A truck can carry up to eight cameras for a full view around the vehicle.

Video and telematics data upload to the cloud, where they become safety events that a review team turns into driver coaching material. A maintenance module watches the chassis, body and equipment continuously. It hands mechanics a list of repairs ranked by severity or by how long remains before failure. Other modules take on tax paperwork, recording the data behind IFTA reporting and excise fuel tax recovery.

Contamination detection spots recycling contamination and other non-conforming refuse at the point of collection. Adding the route review module helps haulers plan and report the annual reviews that California State Bill 1383 requires. Container quality reviews photograph and geolocate each collection event to find carts needing repair or replacement. The company presents itself as part of Environmental Solutions Group alongside Soft-Pak and Heil, under the Connected Collections banner. Equipment can be taken monthly rather than bought outright, on what the company calls a Hardware as a Service model.
